newsitem.title: USA: Cano Limon field could be back up today -- Oxy.
newsitem.headline: Cano Limon field could be back up today -- Oxy.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp said it could restart operations on the Cano Limon oil field in Colombia pending confirmation that the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline had suffered no further rebel attacks.
"We could be up and running today," a company spokesman said. "The lifting of force majeure is contingent on confirmation that there are no additional breaches."

Pumping on the pipeline resumed this morning after repairs were completed, but field storage of around 450,000 barrels would have to be drawn down before operations could get fully underway, the spokesman said.

Occidental cut daily production from about 175,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 70,000 bpd after the first of two pipeline bombings on July 6. It then shut in the field completely on July 10 after a second attack.
On July 15, Oxy declared force majeure on the field, the first time ever since it came on-stream, announcing it was temporarily laying off as many as 200 employees and contract workers.
On July 6, Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol declared force majeure on crude loadings at the Caribbean port of Caovenas, a measure that often occurs in line with frequent rebel bombings.
It remained unclear on Friday whether the force majeure on loadings might also be lifted imminently or whether Ecopetrol would wait until a floating storage unit of two million barrels was re-filled.
